listening.title: Negotiating price and terms with a client

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: Thank you for your time, Nam. Shall we talk about price and terms today?

lines.speaker: Nam (Procurement Manager)
lines.text: Yes, please. Can you give me a ballpark figure for one hundred licences?

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: For that volume, our price point is about twenty dollars per user each month.

lines.speaker: Nam (Procurement Manager)
lines.text: That is higher than our budget. Is there any wiggle room on that number?

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: A little, if we increase the contract length from one year to two years.

lines.speaker: Nam (Procurement Manager)
lines.text: So the trade-off is a lower price but a longer commitment. I understand.

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: Exactly. With two years I can offer eighteen dollars and free training for your staff.

lines.speaker: Nam (Procurement Manager)
lines.text: What about payment? We prefer not to make a large upfront payment.

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: We can split it into four quarterly payments with no extra charge.

lines.speaker: Nam (Procurement Manager)
lines.text: Good. But please remove the penalty clause if we cancel after eighteen months.

lines.speaker: Linh (Sales Executive)
lines.text: I must check with my manager, but I think we can agree in principle today.
